newsitem.title: USA: Nearby CME live, feeder cattle months end higher.
newsitem.headline: Nearby CME live, feeder cattle months end higher.

text.p: A late round of light commercial buying buoyed nearby CME live and feeder futures contracts to higher closes after they traded lower most of the session.

Traders believing there will be a long-term rise in cash cattle prices, led the buying, floor sources said. Other traders, who remain bearish, expect lower cattle prices next week avoided trading during the late rally.
Cargill, Lind-Waldock, and Paine Webber were late buyers which lifted April higher.
"The floor was short and there was nothing to stop it (from going up)," said a cattle trader.
"The feeling still is, it (the cattle market) will be $62 next week," he said.
Cash cattle traded this week at $63.00, and some CME traders forecasted $64.00 trades next week.
"We were oversold and it is snowing in Amarillo," said another trader explaining the late rally.

A winter storm entered Texas early Thursday and should spread into western Oklahoma and western Kansas, bringing three to five inches of snow. Winter storms can slow cattle weight gains and delay marketings, but meteorologists said the latest storm should not seriously affect cattle there because the snow was not accompanied by extremely low temperatures.

Feeder cattle largely followed live cattle, traders said. Lower CBOT corn futures also encouraged buying in March and April feeder cattle. Refco was a late buyer of March against selling by Smith Barney, traders said.

A firm tone to cash feeder cattle markets encouraged light buying. USDA reported steady to $3.00 higher cash feeder prices Wednesday at the Amarillo market, and $1.00 higher prices at Oklahoma City early this week.
Live cattle closed up 0.375 to down 0.450 cent with February up 0.225 at 63.975 and April was up 0.375 at 65.925. Feeder cattle closed up 0.275 to down 0.450 cent with March up 0.275 at 68.675.
